items.a: One digital file without watermark: a JPEG in sRGB, {square} for one eye and {px} on the longest side for several eyes, made in full resolution from the preview you approve. After you pay, your order page opens and its link comes by email. It is usually ready within minutes; if we ever hold an order for a check, the latest we promise is {hours} hours. It stays available to download for 12 months. A personal licence: print it for yourself or as a gift; selling the artwork or prints is not included (see the terms of sale).

items.q: Do you print or ship it?
items.a: No. Printing is not part of your order: a print shop charges for it separately, and its price depends on the shop, the size and the material. If we ever add printing, we will say so on this page.

items.q: Can I print it, and how big?
items.a: Yes. Choose a print shop, pick a square size such as 20, 30, 40 or 50 cm and upload the JPEG. For other shapes ask the shop to crop or add a border, and ask for a proof or a sample. We do not print or ship: the print is the shop's work and price. For one eye we recommend up to {printMax}, which is about 208 pixels per inch (about 347 at 30 cm). Print shops usually ask for about 150 to 300. With several eyes the long edge can be up to {printMaxCm}. Above {printMaxCm} a print is possible but stretches the file further, so we do not promise it. The result also depends on your photo.

items.q: Will my print look like the pictures?
items.a: The pictures of rooms, hands and prints are visualisations of how a file can look once printed, not photographs. A real print differs with the print shop, the material and the light in your room, the same way a screen differs from a wall, and its colours can differ from your screen. Sizes in the pictures are illustrative, and some styles in them open soon. Ask the print shop for a proof or a sample.

We start from your own photo and clear away reflections. Where your phone could not capture the finest fibres, our AI restores them, so the very finest detail is a reconstruction, not a microscope photograph. In some styles the powder, liquid, flame or dust around your iris is AI-made material from a shared library, so another customer's artwork can contain the same piece. Your iris keeps the colours, the pattern and the layout of your photo; the finest fibres are restored by AI, as described above. The rooms, hands and objects in the pictures on this page are made with AI, not photographed. The eyes on this page are our own and example photos, never a customer's, all taken with care: your result depends on your photo, and the free preview shows it before you pay.

items.q: What if my photo is bad?
items.a: Before you pay, the preview tells you if a shot is too blurry, too dark or the pupil too wide, and shows you how to retake it. Still stuck? Email your best photos to {email} and we will look at them.

items.q: What if I do not like the result?
items.a: You see your own preview free before you pay, and after you pay we start making your file at once. If the file is defective or clearly differs from the preview you approved, write to us: we render it again or refund you. Details on withdrawal are below.

items.q: Which phone and camera should I use?
items.a: Any recent smartphone with a good back camera. Use the back camera at 2x or 3x zoom, not the selfie camera. Use daylight from a window or a torch, off to one side, not a room lamp or the flash. Hold the phone about 10 cm from your eye, tap the iris to focus, keep the eye wide open so no lid or lashes cross the iris, take glasses off and take three to five shots. We measure every shot and use the sharpest.

items.q: Will the colour match my eye?
items.a: The colour comes from your photo, and a phone records colour differently under a room lamp, a flash or in shade. We never recolour an iris, so if a photo looks tinted, retake it in window daylight or with a torch from the side.

items.a: Acrylic is glossy and deep; hang it away from direct window glare. Aluminium is crisp and modern. Canvas is soft with less glare, but its weave softens the finest fibres. A framed print is classic. An acrylic block stands on a shelf. For a phone, add black space around the square file in any photo editor and set it as your wallpaper. The details on this page are typical of print shops and vary; ask the print shop for a sample.

items.q: Can I withdraw from an order?
items.a: We start making your file as soon as your order confirmation email has gone out, normally within a minute of your payment. Before paying, you agree that we start straight away, so the 14-day right of withdrawal ends once we have started making your file. Until then you can withdraw by email or online with "Withdraw from contract here", at the foot of this page or through the withdrawal link in your order confirmation email. If your file is defective or clearly differs from the preview you approved, write to us: we render it again or refund you. The details are in our terms of sale and the withdrawal information, linked at the foot of this page.
